comments.text: Are you using spaces as a separator option? Try disabling that
There isn't an option for that when I open the file
When you double click the file on your file manager, isn't this screen that pops up? There is Separator Option there.
Just noticed, that mine have a "Always show on import" marked there, so, you maybe uncheck that in the past, and LibreOffice is using de last option set then. Look up on how to re-enabled that.

I did a double check, and it looks like this is due to the different episode numbering between TV Time and TMDB.

On TV Time, episode 4 is split into two separate episodes (Part 1 and Part 2), while on TMDB it is listed as a single episode. This shifts the numbering, which affects all the imported comments after episode 5.

I also noticed that the same issue occurs with episode 16.

Hope this helps!

Italian: "trackerati" should be "tracciati"

‘Tracciati’ sounds more natural because it is an Italian word, but it doesn’t fully convey the intended meaning. ‘Tracciati’ sounds closer to ‘trackati’, which is an adapted loanword (or morphologically adapted anglicism) from English and is sometimes heard in contexts like video games. Personally, I would prefer something like ‘registrati’.

**Watched and rated 8/10**

**Watched 7/10**

The "and rated" part is missing.

Watched 2 episodes

There is no indication that both episodes were also rated.

Example:
I watched a Rick and Morty episode.
Later, I rated that episode.
However, the rating entry appears below the watch entry, even though it happened later.

As far as I remember, this was previously fixed/removed because it cluttered the activity (watch) feed.

Thanks for the great work on the new Journal!

bugs.title: watched history VS recent activity/journal1 VS profile journal2
bugs.body:
[identity removed]
Device: iPhone 13mini 
OS: iOS 26.5.2 (23F84)
App version: Refract v1.6.703-019fbeb9

I’m posting this in BUG REPORT, SUGGESTIONS, and DATA as I believe it’s related and relevant to all three. 

(For the purposes of this report I have designated names to the two distinctly independent journals for clarity)

As the title implies.. watched history differs from recent activity/journal and full history journal. 

Secondly… why are there two distinctly different “journals” ? One accessed within:
CONTINUE —> WATCHED HISTORY—>SEE FULL HISTORY —> JOURNAL 1

and the second accessed within:
PROFILE —> RECENT ACTIVITY —> JOURNAL 2

One would expect that these 3 histories be identical to one another and intrinsically linked. Watched history tends to be absent of random content, thus creating a chaotic amalgamation of events. Journal 1 has an episode count on the associated show and Journal 2 has the most desirable information chronicling flow… listing each episode of whatever show or movie in the order it was watched. This is evidenced in the 3 pictures comparing Avatar The Last Airbender records between those two spaces. 

Unfortunately , recent activity/journal2… although much more accurate in its record keeping chronology, seems to have its own quirks when it comes to recording a movie watching event, as you can see it tripled those 2 events associated with Masters of the Universe and Dust Bunny.

bugs.body:

comments.text: Hi [mention removed], welcome! Could you send me your export file in DM so I check what's happening?
Done
https://www.thetvdb.com/series/superstore/seasons/official/2 https://www.themoviedb.org/tv/62649-superstore/season/2

So what's happening here is a matching problem between the two databases we use. TV Time tracks everything using TVDB, but Refract runs on TMDB, and these two databases don't always agree on how episodes are numbered.

For Superstore specifically: TVDB treats the "Olympics" episode as a Special (S00E01), so it counts Season 2 as 21 episodes starting with "Strike". TMDB on the other hand follows NBC's official listing and puts "Olympics" as S02E01, making Season 2 22 episodes. When we import your watch history, we match episode-by-episode by number — so our S2E1 maps to their S2E1, and so on. Because of that one offset, the very last episode of Season 2 ("Tornado", E22 on TMDB) never gets matched and stays unwatched. That's exactly what your screenshot shows!

For the anime issue: TVDB splits anime by Japanese cour (typically 12-13 episodes per season), while TMDB often groups everything into one big Season 1. So your watched history from TV Time covers "Season 1" in TVDB terms (12 eps), but on TMDB that's just the first half of a 25-episode season. The second half has no match and stays unchecked.

Both issues come from the same root cause: two databases, two different ways of organizing the same show, no universal standard between them.
For more info on why we decided to use TMDB and not TVDB: https://discord.com/channels/1490347491151970366/1493662414846169129/1493664252752429176

Also we're planning to build our own matching database to bridge TVDB and TMDB properly to handle those edge cases. It's going to take a fair amount of time to get right, but it's the only real long-term fix. We'll keep you posted as things improve, and in the meantime, you can manually mark those episodes as watched directly in the app!
Hope it helped! Even though we cannot really fix that for now.

bugs.title: TMDB - 'Season finale' episode type not honored within Refract
bugs.body:
I watch quite a few small series where the initial episode count is assumed to be 10. Someone creates a TMDB page for the show and sets it to 10 episodes. Which was later-on turns out to be not correct, a change is made to TMDB where episode 8 gets a 'Season Finale' tag and the air dates of episode 9 & 10 are removed.

Refract still shows all 10 episodes and does not 'update/fix' it's database to reflect these changes (other trackers such as 'Movie Paradise' do reflect these changes so there is a method for this to work).
Adding a new episode to a TMDB series gets added into refract usually by the next day. This 'season finale' and air dates removal of episodes which will never air is not done during the 'nightly fix' (waited 3 days before this report to see if this change is carried out during the nightly fix/update).

PS; Getting an episode deleted from TMDB is an enormous pain/hassle and is never done/priority for small series (think only couple thousand people watch it) for those maintaining TMDB. Therefore this 'Season Finale' edit is the most practical one within TMDB. Please add this to the nightly fix workflow.
Thank you for all the work put into the app ❤️

Okay I've got logged out and found the thing. It might be one of them, other logouts may occur but this one will normally not happen again.

Explanation for those who are technically interested:
*When you reopen Refract after a long break, your login token (which lives for 5 minutes max) has expired. 

Two things happen at once — the app tries to refresh your token, and Refract tries to fetch your latest data. 

It's a race. Most of the time the token refresh wins. But sometimes the data fetch wins, hits the server with the old expired token, gets rejected, and the app thinks "guess they're logged out" → boom, login screen.

The fix: when you come back to the app, we now wait for a fresh token before fetching anything else. Takes less than a second usually, completely invisible. In rare cases (slow network), you might see a brief "loading" moment instead of being logged out. 

Much better tradeoff.*

I think I figured at least 1 variable. 
If you don't leave any empty line you will get the text cut off.

You need to have at least 2 paragraphs.

If you do two jump lines (leaving one empty) THEN you get the option to make the window bigger.
Replies to comments only showing 2 lines still:
So this doesn’t really work well, because if your comment is slightly “too long”, you can’t send the reply through (something TV Time had issues with as well).

I would need to see the original message you wrote to know if it really doesn't works.

The important part is to have an empty line and text after it. So it counts as a new paragraph.

"Blabla
 < - empty, just a line jump
Blablabla" <- more text

Or even

"Blablabla
 < - empty, just a line jump
." <- more text

For me this workaround has been working.
In any case it's just a workaround. It shouldn't be necessary to be able to read full answers.

So the issue isn’t so much that your workaround doesn’t work. It’s that if you go beyond like 12 lines, the send button disappears, making your workaround unnecessary. bugs.title: "Unknown" Watch Date Still Stores a Time
bugs.body:
When setting the watch date of a movie or TV show to "Unknown", the application still assigns the current time at the moment the unknown date is saved.
This creates inaccurate data in statistics related to watch times, because entries with an unknown watch date should not contribute to hourly viewing statistics.
Why this is a problem
I currently have around 140 movies that need to be marked as Unknown. Previously, when importing my watch history to TV Time, all imported movies were assigned to the same date, which completely distorted my statistics. I want to avoid the same issue in Refract by marking those entries as having an unknown watch date.
However, because Refract still stores the current time when "Unknown" is selected, all of those movies end up being recorded as watched at the exact hour I edited them. As a result, the hourly viewing statistics become heavily skewed.

Is there something we do about it besides manual fixes? We're talking a potentially significant number episodes that it claims were imported but don't show as watched. For example the entire season 2 of Apothecary Diaries was listed as unwatched after the import despite the episode count warning showing `TV Time 48 eps, TMDB 49 eps`. But only ~half of those actually showed as watched. Scrolling though my "Continue" list shows a large amount of my anime only having been watched through the end of season 1 despite me being up to date with one or more seasons after that. 

I realize the various ways anime is cataloged is a hellscape. Even between trackers that group all seasons into one show (TV Time, Trakt) and those that tend to separate them into separate shows (MAL, Anilist) do so differently from each other. But I'm still hoping something can be done in an automated fashion to resolve this.

also if you want to know all the missmatch quicly and do it manually I did this: https://canary.discord.com/channels/1490347491151970366/1491221394644668469/1525585578450620527

bugs.title: Crash Report – Ici tout commence Season 1
bugs.body:
🇫🇷

Lorsque j'ouvre la saison 1 de Ici tout commence, Refract plante systématiquement.

Le problème semble venir du fait que TMDB renvoie toujours la structure par défaut avec seulement deux saisons contenant plus de 1 000 épisodes chacune. Le chargement d'une liste aussi volumineuse provoque un ralentissement important, puis un crash de l'application.

La prise en charge des TMDB Episode Groups permettrait d'utiliser la véritable organisation des saisons (Saison 1, 2, 3, etc.), de réduire le nombre d'épisodes chargés simultanément et d'éviter ce problème.

Episode Group concerné :
https://www.themoviedb.org/tv/112470-ici-tout-commence/episode_group/6865862ce3fc54222031f6e4

🇬🇧

Opening Season 1 of Ici tout commence consistently crashes Refract.

The issue appears to be caused by TMDB's default season structure, which still contains only two seasons with over 1,000 episodes each. Loading such a large episode list causes major slowdowns and eventually crashes the app.

Supporting TMDB Episode Groups would use the correct season structure (Season 1, 2, 3, etc.), dramatically reduce the number of loaded episodes, and likely prevent this crash.

Hey yeah thanks, it's actually an issue when changing devices during an update - I think.

Steps to fix "Can't log in" on Android:

1. Go to Settings → Apps → Refract
Tap Storage → Clear Data (this is different from uninstalling — it wipes the broken keychain)
2. Restart your tablet
3. Reinstall Refract from the Play Store

Try signing in again

If it still fails after that, let us know your Android version — some very old Android versions have a known bug with secure key storage that may need a different workaround.

comments.text:
[name removed] [REFR], Role icon, 🧠 The Architect — 10:58
Why more episodes show up in your yearly 2026 count

When you import from another app, all your episodes usually arrive with the exact same timestamp — the moment of the import. To stop that from flooding the yearly goal (imagine 875 Pokémon episodes all counted as "watched today"), we ignore any group of 5+ episodes of the same show that share the exact same second.

The problem was that marking a season inside Refract does the same thing: all episodes get one identical timestamp. So marking a 41-episode season counted as zero toward your goal.

Since 30 July, the rule only applies to imported episodes. Episodes you mark yourself in the app always count, even a whole season at once.

That's why your 2026 count includes the episodes you bulk-marked on 9–10 July: One Piece (189), Naruto Shippūden (86) and Sweet Home (8) — 283 in total, all stamped with the moment you marked them. They're counted as "watched in 2026" because that's the only date we have for them. If you give them real dates, they'll move to the right year.

Separately: the number your app is showing you is also too high on top of that — that part is a bug on our side and we're fixing it.

bugs.body:
In this days I tried to figure out why the number of episodes imported correctly with a json file didn't match the number of total episodes in the stats. 

The result is: Episode Count doesn't Include on hold series!

Possible explanation: I noticed than if in a json file the status is "on hold", in Refract they go in the "planned to watch" (watch later in json) 

Vice versa, if in the json the status is "watch later" (planned to watch on Refract) the series go to on hold section.

Final explanation: the episode count doesn't include planned to watch series because they have 0 episodes. But With this status being mistakenly reversed, the episode count is actually excluding on hold series Believing that they are the planned to watch ones!

comments.text: In reality it's just 1 bug: planned to watch and on hold are basically inverted, so episode count is reading planned to watch (the one with zero episodes) and excluding on hold (the one with episodes seen)

I forgot to say one thing. You know that the number of episodes in the statistics inexplicably changes all the time? Here is a cause that can be precisely this. Just remove/pause a TV series and the stats change
[mention removed] can you remind me your username?
I'll have a look today
andreox8 (found in one of his older posts)
You're right [mention removed] , both will be fixed soon!

What changed — both halves of the fraction now cover the same set of shows:

* Pausing a show no longer changes the number. The watched count used to skip on-hold shows while the total it was shown against included them; both now cover every library status.
* Shows with an unknown episode total count their watched episodes instead of contributing zero, so the figure stops jumping whenever background metadata enrichment lands. Their unknown total falls back to their own watched count, so the fraction can still never exceed 100%.
* The TV and Anime sub-rows follow the same rule, and older app versions reading the legacy total fields get the same coherent pair rather than a mixed one.
* The cached stats snapshot version was bumped, so existing users get the corrected number on their next Stats visit with no action.

Verified on the live database for you: 12,482 episodes, up from 12,196 — +189 recovered from 16 paused shows and +97 from shows with unknown totals

- Your yearly goal uses the watch date saved for each item.

Red Letter Media

bugs.title: Feature Request: Idempotent re-imports / Skipping already imported shows
bugs.body:
Hey! I noticed that some shows were skipped during the migration because the total episode counts didn't match 100% between TV Time and TMDB. Here are a few examples from my logs:

Will it be possible in the future to re-run the full JSON import to grab only these missing/skipped titles? It would be great if the importer could act idempotently—skipping already successfully migrated shows without creating duplicates, so we can safely retry the files once the mapping or episode-match logic gets updated.

As a UI/UX improvement for this, maybe we could have a "Import missing only" checkbox on the import page.

Also, it would be awesome to display the current number of users in the queue on the frontend. That way, a user can immediately see how backed up the system is and decide whether it makes sense to jump in line right away or wait a bit.

bugs.title: Import silently drops episodes when TVDB series maps to multiple TMDB entries
bugs.body:
--------------------------
Read the #data-issues notice — this isn't missing data (both DBs are correct), it's the import pipeline not handling the TVDB/TMDB structural discrepancy.
--------------------------
[identity removed]

**Description**

When importing a TV Time Out JSON export, episodes in a season that TVDB tracks under one entry — but TMDB splits into a separate standalone series — are silently dropped with no warning.

**Concrete example**

- Series: Berlin (Money Heist spin-off, Netflix)
- TVDB: both seasons under ID 413033
- TMDB: split into two entries — Season 2 isErmine (2026), TMDB 308014, IMDB tt42178219

{
 "title": "Berlin (2023)",
 "id": { "tvdb": 413033, "imdb": null },
 "seasons": [
 { "number": 1, "episodes": [ ...8 episodes... ] },
 { "number": 2, "episodes": [ ...8 episodes... ] }
 ]
}

Expected: Season 2 episodes imported and mat
Actual: Season 1 imports correctly. Season 2 silently dropped — no error, no warning.

**Root cause hypothesis**

Import resolves tvdb: 413033 to its TMDB cousodes that don't belong to that entry. Season 2 lives under a separate TMDB entry (308014) so it has no matching context.

**Suggested fix**

On TVDB→TMDB season mismatch, attempt a secondary lookup via individual TVDB episode IDs, or at minimum warn the user
about unmatched episodes.

**Workaround**

Manually create a separate JSON with the correct title, seasons renumbered from 1, and re-import.
